title: Find an episode to talk about
intro: Answer a few questions about someone, or about yourself. We'll write a prompt for your own AI assistant, and it will suggest podcast episodes worth talking about. Your answers stay in this browser.

questions.label: What do they watch, read or listen to now?
questions.labelSelf: What do you watch, read or listen to now?
questions.hint: For example: cable news, cooking shows, true crime.
questions.promptLine: What they watch, read or listen to now: {answer}
questions.promptLineSelf: What I watch, read or listen to now: {answer}

questions.label: What do they bring up at dinner?
questions.labelSelf: What do you bring up at dinner?
questions.hint: For example: their garden, the school board, a book they loved.
questions.hintSelf: For example: your garden, the school board, a book you loved.
questions.promptLine: What they bring up at dinner: {answer}
questions.promptLineSelf: What I bring up at dinner: {answer}

questions.label: What have they already heard every argument about?
questions.labelSelf: What have you already heard every argument about?
questions.hint: Leave it blank if nothing comes to mind.
questions.promptLine: Already heard every argument about, so avoid: {answer}
questions.promptLineSelf: Already heard every argument about, so avoid: {answer}

options.label: They should: they get to teach
options.prompt: them, so they get to teach me
options.promptSelf: me, because I know this subject well

options.label: Something new, where I'd want their thinking
options.prompt: something new to them, where I'd want their thinking

options.label: A careful look at something they care about
options.labelSelf: A careful look at something I care about
options.prompt: a careful look at something they care about
options.promptSelf: a careful look at something I care about

questions.label: Where and how will they be listening?
questions.labelSelf: Where and how will you be listening?
questions.hint: Say it your way, or tap one of these.

questions.label: How long will they give it?
questions.labelSelf: How long will you give it?

friend.opening: I want to send a friend one podcast episode that we'll both have something to say about. Help me pick.
friend.closing:
Suggest 3 or 4 specific episodes (not shows). Put each on one line in this form:
Show — Episode title | length | clean or explicit | suggested timestamp for my comment | link
Use an Apple Podcasts episode link when you can. For a Substack, give the post link. One link per line, nothing else on the line after the link.
Under each episode line, add one line starting "Why:" with one sentence on why it suits them and one question I could end my comment with.
Before you answer, look up each link and confirm it opens that exact episode. Never write a link from memory or guess an ID. If you can't confirm an episode link, give the show's Apple Podcasts link and add (show link) before it.

self.opening: I want one podcast episode for myself that I'll have something to say about. Help me pick.
self.closing:
Suggest 3 or 4 specific episodes (not shows). Put each on one line in this form:
Show — Episode title | length | clean or explicit | suggested timestamp for my comment | link
Use an Apple Podcasts episode link when you can. For a Substack, give the post link. One link per line, nothing else on the line after the link.
Under each episode line, add one line starting "Why:" with one sentence on why it suits me and one question I could think about at that moment.
Before you answer, look up each link and confirm it opens that exact episode. Never write a link from memory or guess an ID. If you can't confirm an episode link, give the show's Apple Podcasts link and add (show link) before it.

followUp.opening: These links didn't open the episode you named:
followUp.closing: For each one, look up the episode again and give its Apple Podcasts episode link, confirmed, in the same one-line form. Never guess a link.

noneWorked: None of these links opened an episode. Turn on web search in your assistant, then paste its new answer here.
